title: THE BLAME PIE
name: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Own your real share of a problem without carrying everyone else's.
steps:
1. Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Focus only on your true share.
5. Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

win: Responsibility shrank to your actual slice, and one repair matched only what belonged to you.

title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
name: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
goal: Choose the next hour by direction, not by the loudest thought.
steps:
1. Picture two arrows.
2. One arrow shows the next hour if you obey the thought. The other shows the hour if you follow a chosen value.
3. Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select by direction, not by mental volume.

title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
goal: Test each leading option briefly to learn from your reaction without committing.
steps:
1. Picture the two leading options. Mentally fade one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Bring that option back. Repeat once with the other option faded so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
numberedSteps:
1. Picture the two leading options. Mentally fade one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Bring that option back. Repeat once with the other option faded so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
numbered_steps:
1. Picture the two leading options. Mentally fade one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Bring that option back. Repeat once with the other option faded so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
win: Each option was removed and restored once, giving you new data for the next responsible move.
mindBend: Relief or disappointment after a temporary loss can reveal preference without pretending emotion is a final verdict.
mind_bend: Relief or disappointment after a temporary loss can reveal preference without pretending emotion is a final verdict.
formulaFlow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next

title: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
name: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
goal: Let a chosen quality guide the next move before certainty arrives.
steps:
1. Ask, “What quality should the next action carry?” Choose honesty, courage, care, fairness, or patience.
2. Define one visible movement that expresses that quality today.
3. Let certainty remain absent while the chosen quality gives direction.
numberedSteps:
1. Ask, “What quality should the next action carry?” Choose honesty, courage, care, fairness, or patience.
2. Define one visible movement that expresses that quality today.
3. Let certainty remain absent while the chosen quality gives direction.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Build a response that respects both the feeling and the verified facts.

STEPS
1. Complete three lines.
2. FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Read only the third line before acting.

WIN
Your final response included the emotion's need without letting it overwrite reality.

MIND BEND
Wisdom is not the midpoint between feeling and fact. It is the response that can hold both without confusing them.

FORMULA FLOW
Open Voices → Name Feeling → Name Facts → Build Wisdom → Use Wisdom

SAFETY
PAUSE
Delay major action if either witness is too impaired to give usable information.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FEELING OR FIXING?
name: FEELING OR FIXING?
goal: Decide whether the remaining problem needs calming, action, or support.
steps:
1. After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
2. Ask if one specific action could change it.
3. If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.

2. Ask if one specific action could change it.
3. If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. If no, return to acceptance or support.

win: After the body settled, you could tell whether there was a practical door that needed a key.

title: FINISH THE LOOK
name: FINISH THE LOOK
goal: Let your eyes finish checking the present before deciding where attention belongs.
steps:
1. Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. End by selecting where attention belongs now.

title: ONE NOTCH, NOT THE STORY
name: ONE NOTCH, NOT THE STORY
goal: Lower the current alarm one notch without touching the memory itself.
steps:
1. Rate the current alarm from 0 to 10 without explaining why.
2. Pick one present-day cue: your feet, cool water, a stable surface, or a familiar voice.
3. Use that cue for twenty seconds while keeping your eyes open.
4. Rate the alarm once more and stop; no memory review is required.

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
name: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Strengthen one real body signal of steadiness instead of searching only for what feels wrong.
steps:
1. Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add only that support.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
name: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Let breathing happen by itself while you simply notice its movement.
steps:
1. Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

title: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
name: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
goal: Settle into an easy breathing rhythm before changing depth or volume.
steps:

3. Keep the same comfortable rhythm for four more cycles.
4. Drop the counting and allow one natural breath.

title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
name: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
goal: Test which identity claims still make sense across waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
steps:
1. Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.

title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
name: BRAID THE SIGNALS
goal: Let two competing signals share attention before deciding which one matters.
steps:
1. Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide only after the braid is complete.

title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
ritual_name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
goal: Match two sides of physical pressure, then lower both together back to zero.
steps:
1. Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

plain:
MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Match two sides of physical pressure, then lower both together back to zero.

STEPS
1. Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

WIN
Equal resistance stepped down through lighter levels until your hands rested and the urge to press could be checked.

MIND BEND
The body can learn release through symmetry. Lowering matched pressure together shows that stopping does not require one side to lose.

FORMULA FLOW
Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero

SAFETY
PAUSE
Avoid this with pain, hand or joint injury, numbness, breath holding, or any unsafe physical symptom.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Promises, tasks, questions, decisions, and waiting items became a bounded inventory with a later processing time.

Overload feels infinite when the mind cannot see the edges. Counting first turns 'everything' into a finite set.

Question Task → Use Line → Imagine Boundary

PAUSE

title: THE BORING DOSE

goal: Practise a small, fixed dose of boredom without adding stimulation or extending the challenge.
steps:
1. Choose a safe boring task and decide on ten slow breaths.
2. Decide that no extra stimulation will be added during those breaths.
3. Notice boredom’s body sensations until the tenth breath.
4. Stop there, even if you could continue; increase future doses slowly.

title: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
name: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
goal: Stop when your thinking quality clearly drops and keep the last conclusion you could still trust.
steps:
1. Pick your warning signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower understanding, repeated searches, or no new ideas.
2. When two signs appear, stop and keep the last reliable conclusion.
3. Rest before reopening the issue.

45–60 seconds

GOAL
Stop when your thinking quality clearly drops and keep the last conclusion you could still trust.

STEPS
1. Pick your warning signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower understanding, repeated searches, or no new ideas.
2. When two signs appear, stop and keep the last reliable conclusion.
3. Rest before reopening the issue.

WIN
Two warning signs ended the thinking round before more searching could make it worse.

MIND BEND
Past a certain point, more thinking can make certainty stronger while accuracy gets weaker. Stopping can protect the best answer you already reached.

FORMULA FLOW
Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery

SAFETY
PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
ritual_name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Review only the turning point slowly enough to keep observation separate from motive.
steps:
1. Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.

4. Keep that one fact. End the review before building another explanation.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
name: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
numberedSteps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
numbered_steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

goal: Map the full trigger-to-result loop and change one link instead of fighting the whole system.

name: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
ritual_name: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
goal: Borrow one useful behaviour from an imagined capable figure without trying to become them.
steps:

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look.
steps:
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

GOAL
Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look.

STEPS
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

WIN
The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.

MIND BEND
Choice overload shrinks when comparisons are local; deciding between two things is cognitively different from holding the whole field at once.

title: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
name: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
goal: Stop looping over an awkward moment by separating what happened from the extra meaning your mind is adding.
steps:
1. Say the exact words or action you keep running through your mind once, with no commentary.

3. Name the harsh conclusion your mind added afterward.
4. Replace it with the smallest fairer conclusion that still fits the facts.
5. Return to one ordinary action in the present.
